units.description: Encode data as RFC 4648 base64 (section 4: the standard alphabet A-Z a-z 0-9 + /, WITH padding): the text, as ASCII bytes in a heap-owned Buffer (cancho has no string type); the caller drops it. Values 0-25 are A-Z, 26-51 are a-z, 52-61 are 0-9, 62 is '+', 63 is '/'. Every full group of 3 input bytes becomes 4 characters; a final group of 2 bytes becomes 3 characters and one '=', a final group of 1 byte becomes 2 characters and '=='; the empty input gives the empty Buffer. The unused low bits of the last character are zero. No line breaks. Input bytes are 0-255 (int_of(b) is the value). It never fails, and the output length is always 4 * ceil(len(data) / 3).
tests: fn same_bytes[&a, &b](x: &a [byte], y: &b [byte]) -> [] bool { if len(x) != len(y) { return false; } var i = 0; while i < len(x) { if int_of(x[i]) != int_of(y[i]) { return false; } i = i + 1; } return true; }

fn enc_is[&h](heap: &!h Heap, data: &static [byte], want: &static [byte]) -> [heap] int { let b = base64_encode(heap, data); var same = false; borrow b as &x in { same = same_bytes(buffer.bytes(x), want); } buffer.drop(heap, b); if same { return 0; } return 1; }
pub fn test_encode_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(enc_is(heap, "", ""), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_encode_2[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(enc_is(heap, "f", "Zg=="), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_encode_3[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(enc_is(heap, "fo", "Zm8="), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_encode_4[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(enc_is(heap, "foo", "Zm9v"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_encode_5[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(enc_is(heap, "foob", "Zm9vYg=="), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_encode_6[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(enc_is(heap, "fooba", "Zm9vYmE="), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_encode_7[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(enc_is(heap, "foobar", "Zm9vYmFy"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_encode_8[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(enc_is(heap, "Man", "TWFu"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_encode_9[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(enc_is(heap, "Ma", "TWE="), 0); return 0; }

units.description: Strictly decode RFC 4648 base64 (standard alphabet, padded): Ok(the original bytes in a heap-owned Buffer, which the caller drops) exactly when text is what base64_encode would produce for some data, otherwise Err(message). The empty text is Ok(empty). Every one of these is Err, and it must never panic on any bytes: (1) length not a multiple of 4, which includes missing padding ("Zg", "Zm8"); (2) any byte outside A-Z a-z 0-9 + / and the padding '=': '-' and '_' (URL-safe) are outside, and so are space, tab, '\r', '\n' (whitespace is not skipped, anywhere), NUL and bytes of 128 or more; (3) misplaced or wrong padding: '=' anywhere but the last one or two characters of the whole text ("Zg==Zg==", "=AAA", "A=AA"), three or four '=' ("A===", "===="), a lone '=' in third place ("AA=A"); a last group with two data characters must end in exactly "==", one with three in exactly one '='; (4) non-zero trailing bits: in a last group "xy==" the low 4 bits of y's value must be 0 (y is one of A Q g w) and in "xyz=" the low 2 bits of z's value must be 0 (z is one of A E I M Q U Y c g k o s w 0 4 8); "Zh==" and "Zm9=" are Err, "Zg==" and "Zm8=" are Ok. Err carries a static message; it does not matter which. The signature cannot say that decode must not leak: on every Err path nothing is left allocated.
tests: fn same_bytes[&a, &b](x: &a [byte], y: &b [byte]) -> [] bool { if len(x) != len(y) { return false; } var i = 0; while i < len(x) { if int_of(x[i]) != int_of(y[i]) { return false; } i = i + 1; } return true; }

fn dec_is[&h](heap: &!h Heap, text: &static [byte], want: &static [byte]) -> [heap] int { match base64_decode(heap, text) { result.Result::Ok(b) => { var same = false; borrow b as &x in { same = same_bytes(buffer.bytes(x), want); } buffer.drop(heap, b); if same { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }

fn dec_err[&h](heap: &!h Heap, text: &static [byte]) -> [heap] int { match base64_decode(heap, text) { result.Result::Ok(b) => { buffer.drop(heap, b); return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }
pub fn test_decode_ok_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_is(heap, "", ""), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_ok_2[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_is(heap, "Zg==", "f"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_ok_3[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_is(heap, "Zm8=", "fo"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_ok_4[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_is(heap, "Zm9vYmFy", "foobar"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_ok_5[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_is(heap, "TWFu", "Man"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_err_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_err(heap, "Zg"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_err_2[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_err(heap, "Zm9vYg="), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_err_3[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_err(heap, "Zg==\n"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_err_4[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_err(heap, "Zm 9v"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_err_5[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_err(heap, "Zm9-"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_err_6[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_err(heap, "Zg==Zg=="), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_err_7[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_err(heap, "A==="), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_err_8[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_err(heap, "Zh=="), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_decode_err_9[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(dec_err(heap, "Zm9="), 0); return 0; }
